bull_bear.body: Growth funded by mix of internal accruals, existing equity, and debt; INR 100 Cr rights issue raised (INR 35 Cr received in Jan 2026, balance in two calls); No dividend mentioned; Reinvestment into capacity and brand building.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Seasonality in ice cream (Q2/Q3 weakness); Input cost volatility for global commodities; Execution risk on capacity ramp-up; Competition from large FMCG players entering nuts segment; ESOP overhang (though FY27 cost expected < FY26).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, and execution-focused; Emphasis on 'scale with profitability' rather than cash burn; Transparent on one-offs (ESOP) and seasonality.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Ice cream division achieved PAT profitability in FY26 (vs planned FY27); Working capital cycles of nuts (peak in festive) and ice cream (peak in summer) are complementary, optimizing cash flow; 37,000 retail touchpoints of ice cream not yet fully leveraged for nuts cross-selling.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The journey slide records a completed 'Rs 1 billion Rights Issue; initiated capacity expansion and cold-chain scale-up' - i.e. equity raised and deployed into the capacity and freezer build rather than returned.
- Management frames the model as internally funded across engines: 'Krishival Nuts providing a strong cash-generating foundation and Melt N Mellow emerging as the high-growth engine', with 'disciplined execution, prudent capital allocation'.
- Consolidated balance sheet at 31st Mar'26 vs 31st Mar'25 shows the reinvestment: Property, Plant & Equipment Rs 52.52 Cr vs Rs 33.35 Cr, Capital Work-in-progress Rs 10.55 Cr vs Rs 2.22 Cr, Cash and Cash Equivalents Rs 28.31 Cr vs Rs 14.65 Cr, Total Equity Rs 199.91 Cr vs Rs 141.69 Cr.
- Borrowings rose on both tenors: non-current Borrowings Rs 18.16 Cr vs Rs 10.69 Cr and current Borrowings Rs 17.20 Cr vs Rs 1.91 Cr at 31st Mar'26 vs 31st Mar'25 (quoted as the deck's two separate lines; the deck states no combined debt figure and no net-debt or leverage ratio).
- No dividend, buyback or payout policy is mentioned anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Dual-brand model spanning nuts and ice cream reduces dependence on any single product segment and helps offset seasonality-related fluctuations
- Extensive cold-chain infrastructure grown to 15,490 deep freezers, enhancing product availability and last-mile delivery
- Distribution breadth - more than 45,000 retail touchpoints and a presence across 300+ towns and places in India
- Omnichannel reach across general trade, modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce platforms
- Product innovation depth - more than 67 SKUs in nuts and dry fruits and over 189 SKUs in ice cream, with Melt N Mellow among the brands with the highest SKU counts in the Indian ice cream industry
- Diversified sourcing strategy across multiple geographies with integrated supply chain management
- In-house manufacturing with integrated dairy and bakery operations and a dedicated R&D centre for flavour innovation in the ice cream business
- Migration from NSE Emerge SME platform to the Main Board of NSE and BSE with effect from June 20, 2025, expected to enhance capital-market visibility and liquidity
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility — MD&A Risks section explicitly flags volatility in raw material prices as a key exposure. As a processor and trader of cashew kernels and dry fruits, input cost swings pass directly into margins; the Company mitigates through a diversified sourcing strategy across multiple geographies, integrated supply chain management and disciplined cost-control measures.
- Seasonality in certain product categories — Explicitly flagged in the MD&A. Ice cream has historically been a seasonal consumption category and nuts see festive-demand concentration; the dual-brand model spanning nuts and ice cream is stated to provide resilience by helping offset seasonality-related fluctuations.
- Competitive pressure — Explicitly flagged in the MD&A. The Company competes in FMCG categories undergoing rapid organisation and premiumisation, where success depends on brand strength, distribution width and continuous product innovation.
- Geographic concentration of the ice cream business — Melt N Mellow's 34,200-plus retail touchpoints are concentrated across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Goa, and its sole manufacturing facility is at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, leaving the fastest-growing segment exposed to a single region's demand, weather and regulatory conditions.
- Subsidiary funding and contingent credit exposure — The Board approved an additional Rs. 25 Crore loan to Melt 'N' Mellow Foods Private Limited from Rights Issue proceeds, and subsequent to year-end the Company is providing an additional corporate guarantee of up to Rs. 35 Crore for that subsidiary's credit facilities - concentrating parent balance-sheet risk in one partly-owned (52.94%) subsidiary.
- Execution risk on the capacity and cold-chain expansion programme — Growth depends on delivering a phased roadmap to 40 MT per day of nuts capacity over two years, deploying 10,000 additional deep freezers, and opening approximately 25 FOCO parlours in FY27; delay or under-utilisation of the newly commissioned Halkarni facility would weigh on the operating leverage management expects.
- Related-party transaction intensity — The Company transacts with multiple common-director entities (SSBA Innovations, Empyrean Healthcare, Empyrean Enviro, Aikaara Technologies, SSB Capital Advisors, S A Trading) and has approved related party transactions for an aggregate amount up to Rs. 200 Crore subject to member approval - a governance watch-item requiring ongoing Audit Committee oversight.
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical exposure to input costs — The MD&A flags geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, elevated commodity prices, trade fragmentation, energy price volatility, crude oil price volatility and supply-chain disruptions as influencing input costs and inflation across industries including food and FMCG.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Nuts: Revenue ~INR 209 Cr (implied), 15% EBITDA margin, 10% PAT margin, 70% capacity utilization (existing 10 MT/day), targeting 90% in FY27. Ice Cream: Revenue ~INR 95 Cr, 7% EBITDA margin (ahead of plan), 1.7-1.8% PAT margin, 25% capacity utilization (1 lakh litres/day), targeting 100% by Q1 FY29. Ice Cream sales skewed to Q4 (INR 43 Cr in Q4 vs INR 47 Cr in first 9 months).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as 'among India's fastest-growing FMCG companies, specialising in premium nuts, dry fruits, and ice cream', with company positioning stated as 'Leading presence in premium nuts & aspirational ice cream categories'.
- The two engines are framed as seasonally complementary: Q1 is seasonally strong for ice cream on summer demand while nuts sell more in Q2 and Q3 on festive demand, which management says gives 'greater balance to our revenue profile across the year, while also enabling more efficient working capital management'.
- Presence is concentrated in Western and Southern India - the footprint slide names Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Telangana (Hyderabad) and Andhra Pradesh - plus Singapore with 300+ retail touch-points.
- Scale markers cited: 34,200+ retail touch points for nuts & dry fruits, 11,000+ for ice cream, 300+ towns & places, customer retention over 80%, 200+ employees, over 12 years in the industry, and FSSAI / ISO / HACCP certifications.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Subsidiary structure] The ice cream business is run through subsidiary Melt N Mellow Foods Private Limited; the consolidated balance sheet carries a Non Controlling Interest of Rs 7.31 Cr at 31st Mar'26 (Rs 6.59 Cr at 31st Mar'25), and the deck does not state the ownership percentage.
- [Melt N Mellow milestone] The deck states Melt N Mellow 'Achieved EBITDA profitability in FY26, one year ahead of management's original target' and claims it is 'the only major emerging multi-state ice cream brand successfully scaling operations while remaining profitable'.
- [New market] Entered Andhra Pradesh through 3 CNF locations covering Rayalaseema, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, with the 1,780 freezers added in Q1 predominantly deployed there.
- [Headwinds] The deck flags external headwinds during the quarter: 'diesel availability constraints and higher milk prices'.
- [Exports] Singapore appears as a key market with 300+ retail touch-points, and the stated strategy is to 'Strengthen export footprint in Singapore, Japan & the US markets'.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 was a capacity-building year across both verticals. In the nuts and dry fruits business, the Company commissioned a new 35,000 sq. ft. processing facility at Halkarni, Kolhapur, which became operational in April 2026 and doubled nuts processing capacity from 10 MT per day to 20 MT per day; a phased roadmap has been laid out to expand further to 40 MT per day over the next two years. In the ice cream business, subsidiary Melt 'N' Mellow operates a manufacturing facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar with a production capacity of 1 lakh litres per day, supported by integrated dairy and bakery operations and a dedicated R&D centre for flavour innovation. Distribution and cold-chain infrastructure expanded materially: the deep freezer fleet grew to 15,490 units, Krishival Nuts reached over 11,000 retail touchpoints and Melt N Mellow over 34,200 touchpoints across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Goa, with the overall network spanning more than 300 towns and places in India plus an international presence in Singapore. Funding came from a Rs. 100 crore Rights Issue completed during FY26, whose proceeds are being deployed towards capacity expansion, supply-chain strengthening, manufacturing infrastructure and deep freezer network expansion; the Board approved partial utilisation of these proceeds as an additional Rs. 25 Crore loan to Melt 'N' Mellow to strengthen the cold chain through deployment of 10,000 additional deep freezers. Subsequent to year-end the Company is providing an additional corporate guarantee of up to Rs. 35 Crore for credit facilities to Melt 'N' Mellow. For FY27, management plans to continue nuts capacity expansion towards the 40 MT per day target, further expand the deep freezer network, and launch approximately 25 FOCO ice cream parlours under the 'Mellow & Co.' brand across Mumbai and Pune.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural shift in Indian FMCG from unorganised to organised players and from loose to packaged consumption, favouring branded players with wide distribution
- Rising health consciousness, premiumisation and evolving dietary preferences driving dry fruits and nuts consumption beyond festive occasions
- Indian dry fruits and nuts market projected to grow at approximately 8.5%-9.0% CAGR, expanding from approximately USD 2.2 billion in 2025 to nearly USD 4.7 billion by 2034 (source: IMARC, Grand View Research)
- Indian ice cream market projected to grow at approximately 16% CAGR, from approximately USD 3.8 billion in 2025 to nearly USD 14.5 billion by 2034 (source: IMARC, Market Data Forecast)
- Ice cream transitioning from a seasonal consumption category to a year-round indulgence segment, aided by modern retail, quick commerce and improving cold-chain penetration
- Tier II, III and IV cities emerging as significant demand centres on rising digital penetration, improved connectivity and rising discretionary spending
- Growth of e-commerce and quick commerce platforms accelerating the shift towards organised and branded consumption
- Management expects to benefit from increasing operating leverage, stronger brand visibility, expanding distribution reach and improving capacity utilisation
- Margin levers cited: better product mix, operating leverage, supply-chain efficiencies and improving scale across operations
- Melt N Mellow expected to remain a key growth driver, having reached PAT-level profitability one year ahead of management's original target timeline
- India remaining the fastest-growing major economy with moderating inflation supporting household purchasing power and consumption demand
- FY26 marked a transition from an investment phase to a scale-up phase for the Company
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Krishival Foods delivered 48% revenue growth in FY26 with the Melt N Mellow ice cream division achieving PAT profitability a year ahead of schedule (FY27 expected), validating the dual-engine model of stable nuts cash flow and high-growth indulgence. Management guides for 50%+ top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27, driven by capacity ramp-up and distribution deepening, though Q4 margins were temporarily impacted by one-off ESOP costs.

currentContext.expansion: FY26 was a capacity-building year across both verticals. In the nuts and dry fruits business, the Company commissioned a new 35,000 sq. ft. processing facility at Halkarni, Kolhapur, which became operational in April 2026 and doubled nuts processing capacity from 10 MT per day to 20 MT per day; a phased roadmap has been laid out to expand further to 40 MT per day over the next two years. In the ice cream business, subsidiary Melt 'N' Mellow operates a manufacturing facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar with a production capacity of 1 lakh litres per day, supported by integrated dairy and bakery operations and a dedicated R&D centre for flavour innovation. Distribution and cold-chain infrastructure expanded materially: the deep freezer fleet grew to 15,490 units, Krishival Nuts reached over 11,000 retail touchpoints and Melt N Mellow over 34,200 touchpoints across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Goa, with the overall network spanning more than 300 towns and places in India plus an international presence in Singapore. Funding came from a Rs. 100 crore Rights Issue completed during FY26, whose proceeds are being deployed towards capacity expansion, supply-chain strengthening, manufacturing infrastructure and deep freezer network expansion; the Board approved partial utilisation of these proceeds as an additional Rs. 25 Crore loan to Melt 'N' Mellow to strengthen the cold chain through deployment of 10,000 additional deep freezers. Subsequent to year-end the Company is providing an additional corporate guarantee of up to Rs. 35 Crore for credit facilities to Melt 'N' Mellow. For FY27, management plans to continue nuts capacity expansion towards the 40 MT per day target, further expand the deep freezer network, and launch approximately 25 FOCO ice cream parlours under the 'Mellow & Co.' brand across Mumbai and Pune.

risks.note: MD&A Risks section explicitly flags volatility in raw material prices as a key exposure. As a processor and trader of cashew kernels and dry fruits, input cost swings pass directly into margins; the Company mitigates through a diversified sourcing strategy across multiple geographies, integrated supply chain management and disciplined cost-control measures.

Explicitly flagged in the MD&A. Ice cream has historically been a seasonal consumption category and nuts see festive-demand concentration; the dual-brand model spanning nuts and ice cream is stated to provide resilience by helping offset seasonality-related fluctuations.

Explicitly flagged in the MD&A. The Company competes in FMCG categories undergoing rapid organisation and premiumisation, where success depends on brand strength, distribution width and continuous product innovation.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration of the ice cream business
risks.note: Melt N Mellow's 34,200-plus retail touchpoints are concentrated across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Goa, and its sole manufacturing facility is at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, leaving the fastest-growing segment exposed to a single region's demand, weather and regulatory conditions.

risks.risk: Subsidiary funding and contingent credit exposure
risks.note: The Board approved an additional Rs. 25 Crore loan to Melt 'N' Mellow Foods Private Limited from Rights Issue proceeds, and subsequent to year-end the Company is providing an additional corporate guarantee of up to Rs. 35 Crore for that subsidiary's credit facilities - concentrating parent balance-sheet risk in one partly-owned (52.94%) subsidiary.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the capacity and cold-chain expansion programme
risks.note: Growth depends on delivering a phased roadmap to 40 MT per day of nuts capacity over two years, deploying 10,000 additional deep freezers, and opening approximately 25 FOCO parlours in FY27; delay or under-utilisation of the newly commissioned Halkarni facility would weigh on the operating leverage management expects.

The Company transacts with multiple common-director entities (SSBA Innovations, Empyrean Healthcare, Empyrean Enviro, Aikaara Technologies, SSB Capital Advisors, S A Trading) and has approved related party transactions for an aggregate amount up to Rs. 200 Crore subject to member approval - a governance watch-item requiring ongoing Audit Committee oversight.

risks.risk: Macroeconomic and geopolitical exposure to input costs
risks.note: The MD&A flags geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, elevated commodity prices, trade fragmentation, energy price volatility, crude oil price volatility and supply-chain disruptions as influencing input costs and inflation across industries including food and FMCG.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural shift in Indian FMCG from unorganised to organised players and from loose to packaged consumption, favouring branded players with wide distribution
- Rising health consciousness, premiumisation and evolving dietary preferences driving dry fruits and nuts consumption beyond festive occasions
- Indian dry fruits and nuts market projected to grow at approximately 8.5%-9.0% CAGR, expanding from approximately USD 2.2 billion in 2025 to nearly USD 4.7 billion by 2034 (source: IMARC, Grand View Research)
- Indian ice cream market projected to grow at approximately 16% CAGR, from approximately USD 3.8 billion in 2025 to nearly USD 14.5 billion by 2034 (source: IMARC, Market Data Forecast)
- Ice cream transitioning from a seasonal consumption category to a year-round indulgence segment, aided by modern retail, quick commerce and improving cold-chain penetration
- Tier II, III and IV cities emerging as significant demand centres on rising digital penetration, improved connectivity and rising discretionary spending
- Growth of e-commerce and quick commerce platforms accelerating the shift towards organised and branded consumption
- Management expects to benefit from increasing operating leverage, stronger brand visibility, expanding distribution reach and improving capacity utilisation
- Margin levers cited: better product mix, operating leverage, supply-chain efficiencies and improving scale across operations
- Melt N Mellow expected to remain a key growth driver, having reached PAT-level profitability one year ahead of management's original target timeline
- India remaining the fastest-growing major economy with moderating inflation supporting household purchasing power and consumption demand
- FY26 marked a transition from an investment phase to a scale-up phase for the Company

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 was a capacity-building year across both verticals. In the nuts and dry fruits business, the Company commissioned a new 35,000 sq. ft. processing facility at Halkarni, Kolhapur, which became operational in April 2026 and doubled nuts processing capacity from 10 MT per day to 20 MT per day; a phased roadmap has been laid out to expand further to 40 MT per day over the next two years. In the ice cream business, subsidiary Melt 'N' Mellow operates a manufacturing facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar with a production capacity of 1 lakh litres per day, supported by integrated dairy and bakery operations and a dedicated R&D centre for flavour innovation. Distribution and cold-chain infrastructure expanded materially: the deep freezer fleet grew to 15,490 units, Krishival Nuts reached over 11,000 retail touchpoints and Melt N Mellow over 34,200 touchpoints across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Goa, with the overall network spanning more than 300 towns and places in India plus an international presence in Singapore. Funding came from a Rs. 100 crore Rights Issue completed during FY26, whose proceeds are being deployed towards capacity expansion, supply-chain strengthening, manufacturing infrastructure and deep freezer network expansion; the Board approved partial utilisation of these proceeds as an additional Rs. 25 Crore loan to Melt 'N' Mellow to strengthen the cold chain through deployment of 10,000 additional deep freezers. Subsequent to year-end the Company is providing an additional corporate guarantee of up to Rs. 35 Crore for credit facilities to Melt 'N' Mellow. For FY27, management plans to continue nuts capacity expansion towards the 40 MT per day target, further expand the deep freezer network, and launch approximately 25 FOCO ice cream parlours under the 'Mellow & Co.' brand across Mumbai and Pune.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, disciplined, and execution-focused; Emphasis on 'scale with profitability' rather than cash burn; Transparent on one-offs (ESOP) and seasonality.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Dual-brand model spanning nuts and ice cream reduces dependence on any single product segment and helps offset seasonality-related fluctuations
- Extensive cold-chain infrastructure grown to 15,490 deep freezers, enhancing product availability and last-mile delivery
- Distribution breadth - more than 45,000 retail touchpoints and a presence across 300+ towns and places in India
- Omnichannel reach across general trade, modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce platforms
- Product innovation depth - more than 67 SKUs in nuts and dry fruits and over 189 SKUs in ice cream, with Melt N Mellow among the brands with the highest SKU counts in the Indian ice cream industry
- Diversified sourcing strategy across multiple geographies with integrated supply chain management
- In-house manufacturing with integrated dairy and bakery operations and a dedicated R&D centre for flavour innovation in the ice cream business
- Migration from NSE Emerge SME platform to the Main Board of NSE and BSE with effect from June 20, 2025, expected to enhance capital-market visibility and liquidity

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Seasonality in ice cream (Q2/Q3 weakness); Input cost volatility for global commodities; Execution risk on capacity ramp-up; Competition from large FMCG players entering nuts segment; ESOP overhang (though FY27 cost expected < FY26).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Ice cream division achieved PAT profitability in FY26 (vs planned FY27); Working capital cycles of nuts (peak in festive) and ice cream (peak in summer) are complementary, optimizing cash flow; 37,000 retail touchpoints of ice cream not yet fully leveraged for nuts cross-selling.

strategy.body:

- Continue nuts capacity expansion towards a long-term target of 40 MT per day under a phased roadmap
- Deepen market penetration across Tier II, III and IV cities with premium yet affordable products
- Expand the deep freezer / cold-chain network to strengthen presence across core ice cream markets
- Launch approximately 25 Franchise-Owned Company-Operated (FOCO) ice cream parlours under the 'Mellow & Co.' brand …

- [Subsidiary structure] The ice cream business is run through subsidiary Melt N Mellow Foods Private Limited; the consolidated balance sheet carries a Non Controlling Interest of Rs 7.31 Cr at 31st Mar'26 (Rs 6.59 Cr at 31st Mar'25), and the deck does not state the ownership percentage.
- [Melt N Mellow milestone] The deck states Melt N Mellow 'Achieved EBITDA profitability in FY26, one year ahead of management's original target' and claims it is 'the only major emerging multi-state ice cream brand successfully scaling operations while remaining profitable'.
- [New market] Entered Andhra Pradesh through 3 CNF locations covering Rayalaseema, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, with the 1,780 freezers added in Q1 predominantly deployed there.
- [Headwinds] The deck flags external headwinds during the quarter: 'diesel availability constraints and higher milk prices'.
- [Exports] Singapore appears as a key market with 300+ retail touch-points, and the stated strategy is to 'Strengthen export footprint in Singapore, Japan & the US markets'.

one-line thesis: Krishival Foods delivered 48% revenue growth in FY26 with the Melt N Mellow ice cream division achieving PAT profitability a year ahead of schedule (FY27 expected), validating the dual-engine model of stable nuts cash flow and high-growth indulgence. Management guides for 50%+ top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27, driven by capacity ramp-up and distribution deepening, though Q4 margins were temporarily impacted by one-off ESOP costs.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 304.41 Cr (+48% YoY); EBITDA: INR 41.95 Cr (+66% YoY, 13.78% margin, up 130 bps YoY); PAT: INR 22.2 Cr (+64% YoY, 7.59% margin); Order Book: N/A (FMCG inventory-driven); Net Debt: Funded via internal accruals + INR 100 Cr rights issue (INR 35 Cr received); One-offs: INR 2.88 Cr ESOP cost charged in Q4FY26 (impacted Q4 EBITDA margin; adjusted Q4 EBITDA margin was 12.21% vs 12.03% in Q4FY25).
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~50% for FY27; Bottom-line Growth: 50%+ for FY27; Margins: Nuts steady-state 15%+ EBITDA/10%+ PAT; Ice Cream to reach 14-15% EBITDA at full capacity (Q1 FY29); Order Inflow: N/A; Capex/Commissioning: New 35k sq ft nuts unit commissioned April 2026; 2 lakh sq ft factory under construction.
order book & pipeline: N/A for FMCG; Operational metrics: Ice Cream reached 34,200 retail outlets (15,490 deep freezers); Nuts reached 11,000 touchpoints; Total footprint 300+ Indian towns + Singapore.
segment / subsidiary detail: Nuts: Revenue ~INR 209 Cr (implied), 15% EBITDA margin, 10% PAT margin, 70% capacity utilization (existing 10 MT/day), targeting 90% in FY27. Ice Cream: Revenue ~INR 95 Cr, 7% EBITDA margin (ahead of plan), 1.7-1.8% PAT margin, 25% capacity utilization (1 lakh litres/day), targeting 100% by Q1 FY29. Ice Cream sales skewed to Q4 (INR 43 Cr in Q4 vs INR 47 Cr in first 9 months).
growth verticals / optionality: Mellow & Co. parlours (25 FOCO outlets in FY27 in Mumbai/Pune); Tier 2/3/4 penetration for Nuts; Premium SKUs launch in Ice Cream to counter seasonality; Targeting top 3 ice cream brand status in 7 years; Nuts targeting 10% market share.
margins & cost dynamics: Raw material costs appeared elevated in Q4 due to mix shift toward ice cream (higher RMPM consumption); ESOP cost of INR 2.88 Cr in Q4 distorted margins; Future branding spend to be funded from incremental EBITDA to protect margins.
capex / expansion: INR 25 Cr from rights issue allocated to new 2 lakh sq ft nuts facility in Halkarni MIDC; Phased capacity expansion for Nuts (10 MT -> 20 MT -> 30 MT -> 40 MT over next 3 years); Deep freezer network expansion continuing in FY27.
capital allocation: Growth funded by mix of internal accruals, existing equity, and debt; INR 100 Cr rights issue raised (INR 35 Cr received in Jan 2026, balance in two calls); No dividend mentioned; Reinvestment into capacity and brand building.
risks & watch-items: Seasonality in ice cream (Q2/Q3 weakness); Input cost volatility for global commodities; Execution risk on capacity ramp-up; Competition from large FMCG players entering nuts segment; ESOP overhang (though FY27 cost expected < FY26).
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and execution-focused; Emphasis on 'scale with profitability' rather than cash burn; Transparent on one-offs (ESOP) and seasonality.
non-obvious takeaways: Ice cream division achieved PAT profitability in FY26 (vs planned FY27); Working capital cycles of nuts (peak in festive) and ice cream (peak in summer) are complementary, optimizing cash flow; 37,000 retail touchpoints of ice cream not yet fully leveraged for nuts cross-selling.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.
